segments.text: Yathamcha, Parmapa, the Puravistrasya, I see, Vastu, Sava, Vyat, Yadāpuna, Prasra, Nambavati, Tadā.
Now, the one who is already established in that supreme state of God-consciousness.
To him, where there is no mind, where there is no breath, where there are no thoughts, nothing exists, no senses, only God-consciousness
pervades all around to him.
After a while, Yadāpuna, Prasra, Nambavati, he automatically comes out from Samadhi.
And while he comes out from Samadhi, then what happens to him?
In next sutra, he explains that.
When his breath begins to move out slowly, Samācārya, Yisthācārya.
Then, while his breath moves out slowly towards Vithana, towards outside Samadhi, then Samadarshanam takes place.
Then he sees and he experiences that God-consciousness is pervading outside to.
He feels that God-consciousness is there also existing.
He does not find any difference between Jagrath and Turya.
He does not find any difference between Sopana and Turya.
He does not find any difference between Sushvati and Turya.
Jagrath, Sopana and Sushvati become filled with this state of Turya for him.
Parasuprata ādmakaśārtha parībala samskrtaśya.
The one who is filled with the fragrance of supreme-suprana of God-consciousness.
And his breath is like that.
His breath is filled with that fragrance.
Whose breath comes out slowly from Samadhi, that breathing.
That breathing has some supreme fragrance.
He feels that.
Yogi feels that his breathing has fragrance in him.
Samyak yadī vikaśyata samagra-grantyātmaka antaravastambabala.
Although his breath is moving out.
He feels that his breath is not moving out.
His breath is established already in his supreme being.
So his breath, breath, yeeshat bair mandam chāre prasarane.
His breath comes out very slowly.
Then what he experiences?
Samam.
Samadarshanam.
Chidānanda ganātmata yā ekrupam darshanam samve danam.
He feels that all these three states are filled
with the dense erasā of nectar of God-consciousness.
He comes out of which state?
Hmm?
He comes out in which state?
Dreaming state.
He comes in dreaming state from Samadhi.
No.
So they always come to dreaming state first.
No.
In the beginning.
Not this time.
Not this time.
He is Yogi Raj.
He is King of Yogi.
He comes out in Jagrath also, in wakefulness also.
With this fragrance.
His fragrance is never lost.
His fragrance of God-consciousness.
Yes.
Arat sarvdasasu, I say about the...
It means that his God-consciousness remains in each and every state of his life,
in Jagrath, in Sūpun and in Sūśapti.
It is already explained in Ananda Bairavashastra.
Utsrijya, laukika-charam, adaitam, muktidam, śreth, sarsam, sarvadevāna, tatāvarna,
shrāmadhi, ke, drivāna, samatādarshi, sāmukta, sarvabandani.
Laukika-charam, utsrijya, when the active, daily routine
of his life is over, when he has got over from that daily routine of life,
and he has held the monastic state which gives you, which bestows you final liberation.
Then he saw some of Sarvadevāna.
He is one with each and every devata.
Each and every deity, tatāvarna, shrāmadhi, varan and asam are equal to him.
Brahman, ketra, vāyashin, sudras are equal to him.
drivāna, samatādarshi, what is to be eaten, what is not to be eaten,
what is forbidden to take, what is accepted to be taken.
He doesn't find any difference in these.
Sāmukta, sarvabandani. He is totally liberated from all these bondages, daily life.
He is mukta. Atīvushri, prītbīg gāyām.
In prītbīg yā also, utsvadevā has explained.
Buddha-prāna, prāsarepi, bāhi, deśāyati, upādāna, anahe, sāmko, chāna.
Mishāas, masuru, pula, bheva.
Although he comes out, he comes out in the state of puraśtaka, in the state of prāna
and also in the state of deha.
Although he comes out and flows and works and does all the actions there,
in jagrath, in sopana and sośafti, bāhi, deśāyati, upādāna, anahe, sāmko, chāna.
Those great yogis have not at all any limitation of owning and diswining, pure and impure,
good and bad. This limitation is over for them.
For them, Mishāyati-Masuru pula, bheva.
They attain that supreme universal god consciousness, Mishāyati-Masuru pula bheva.
